answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making each identity post a slashable stake, forfeited when peers prove it faked work. New agents deposit collateral and earn standing only as independent attesters confirm their output over time; clones cannot share that, since each needs its own value at risk. Verified history is the opal in the record, hard to forge; fresh identities sit low on the ridge of trust, throttled until they build a real track record. Votes weigh stake plus age, so new wallets carry little dune of influence. Cost: capital per identity, lost on proven fraud.
